strategy.thesis: Global angel investor network (est. 2000, HQ San Francisco) with a dedicated Japan chapter that began full operations in late 2017; members are accredited angels, family offices and corporate investors who source and co-invest deals, with the global portfolio explicitly spanning Life Sciences (Pharma, Medical Devices, Health IT) alongside tech and consumer — giving the Japan chapter a recurring, if non-exclusive, channel into domestic health-tech deal flow.

summary.en: Japan chapter of the world's largest angel investor network; the global network's stated portfolio explicitly includes life sciences (pharma, medical devices, health IT) alongside other sectors.

strategy.thesis: Family office of the Yamauchi family (Nintendo founding lineage), deploying capital into deep-tech and 'moonshot' ventures spanning aerospace, robotics and next-generation biotechnology. summary.en: Tokyo-based family office of the Nintendo founding Yamauchi family; primarily a generalist deep-tech investor (space, robotics) that has also backed RNA-engineering biotech platform Sixfold Bioscience.

name.local: 公益財団法人難病医学研究財団

strategy.thesis: Public-interest foundation (established Oct. 1973 as the Medical Research Promotion Foundation; renamed to the Japan Intractable Diseases Research Foundation in Sept. 1984; certified as a 公益財団法人 in April 2011) that has run an annual grant competition since 1976 funding basic, clinical and preventive research aimed at elucidating the cause, pathology and treatment of intractable (nanbyo/rare) diseases.

summary.en: A public-interest foundation that has awarded annual research-encouragement grants (¥2M per recipient) to young Japanese researchers and clinicians working on intractable/rare-disease research since 1976.

name.en: Uehara Memorial Foundation for Life Science
name.local: 公益財団法人上原記念生命科学財団

strategy.thesis: Established in February 1985 by Taisho Pharmaceutical to commemorate its 70th anniversary and honor honorary chairman Shokichi Uehara; funds life-science and pharmaceutical research broadly through research grants, the Uehara Prize, international symposia and overseas research fellowships. FY2025 assistance grants (incl. the Uehara Prize subsidiary award) totaled ¥1.3098 billion across 335 cases.

summary.en: A major pharma-founder-endowed foundation (Taisho Pharmaceutical) that has funded broad life-science and drug-development research in Japan since 1985, distributing over ¥1.3 billion annually across hundreds of grants and prizes.

name.local: 公益財団法人武田科学振興財団

strategy.thesis: Public-interest foundation established in 1963 with an endowment from Takeda Pharmaceutical Company; funds original, pioneering medical and life-science research through nine grant programs (e.g. Life Science Research Grants, Medical Research Grants, High-Risk Emerging Infectious Disease Research Grants, Visionary Research Grants). 2024 grants covered 562 awards totaling ¥2.314 billion; cumulative giving since founding reached 11,884 grants totaling ¥43.68 billion.

summary.en: A large, long-running pharma-endowed (Takeda Pharmaceutical) foundation funding medical and life-science research in Japan across nine grant programs, with cumulative giving exceeding ¥43 billion since 1963.
summary.local: 武田薬品工業からの寄付を基に1963年に設立された公益財団。医学・生命科学の独創的・先駆的な研究に広く助成を行っている。
